keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point of the Earth’s surface — not simply straight down, so near a slope the terrain next to you can also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the entity responsible for the obstacle may request permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle’s height.

Registration as a UAS operator is mandatory for drones of 250 g or heavier (or under 250 g with a personal data sensor). Registration is done online on the AACR platform (uas.caa.ro), and the fee is 20 € (MTI Order No. 1280/2021). Your unique operator number (ROU-…) must be displayed on all your drones.

In Romania, the minimum age for a remote pilot is 16 years, or 12 years under the direct supervision of an authorized pilot aged at least 16 years; there is no minimum age for a drone under 250 g in subcategory A1.

No Romanian law generally prohibits flying a drone in built-up areas: the Air Code (Codul aerian, Law 21/2020, Art. 15(2)(d)) exempts drones that comply with European rules, and EASA rules apply in the open category. However, flying over sites of the structures of the national defense, public order and national security system remains prohibited without the written consent of their heads (Art. 15(3)). Above most urban centers there are ROMATSA restricted zones from the ground (GND–120 m AGL), each with the access route indicated in the zone data — usually an MApN approval (aerofoto@mapn.ro) or ATC contact. Check the zone on the map before takeoff.

30 km exclusion zone along the border with UKRAINE (Northern Dobrogea, Sulina–Galați) — flight prohibited by joint order of the Minister of National Defense and the Minister of Transport (Air Code, Art. 15(4))

In the open category, you must keep the drone within your direct line of sight, with the naked eye (glasses/contact lenses are allowed; binoculars or a screen do not count) — or fly with the help of an observer, maintaining clear and effective communication between you at all times, so that together you can monitor the airspace and avoid collisions. Follow-me mode is a separate exception, permitted up to 50 m from the pilot.
Do not fly over assemblies of people. Rules for uninvolved persons depend on subcategory, class mark and operating conditions; check the official matrix.

Flying near airports is prohibited — the protection zones (for example around Henri Coandă Airport in Bucharest) extend for several kilometers. Check the official drone zone map before flying near an airport.
Night flight is permitted under the EASA open-category baseline when the required green flashing light is used, unless a current geographic zone or national rule imposes a stricter condition.

Danube Delta: flying a drone over the reserve requires a permit issued by the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve Administration — on permise.ddbra.ro, under «Permise fotografiere-filmare» (photography/filming permits), there is a «Permis survol dronă de mici dimensiuni (sub 500 g)» (small drone overflight permit, under 500 g) (50 RON); for heavier drones, ask ARBDD. This is an access/photography permit from the administration, not an airspace restriction. In national parks, the park administration’s rules apply.
importantNotes: Registration is 100% online via the AACR portal (uas.caa.ro) — there is no need to travel to Bucharest
The UAS operator registration fee is 20 € under MTI Order No. 1280/2021; the AACR does not publish the fee on its main page — payment is made in the online platform uas.caa.ro.

Recreational flying in cities is not prohibited by law, but in practice most urban centers are in a ROMATSA restricted zone starting from the ground (GND–120 m AGL) — plan your authorization request (usually an MApN approval, aerofoto@mapn.ro) in advance.
The 30 km exclusion zone covers the border with Ukraine (Northern Dobruja), pursuant to a joint MApN–MTI order issued in September 2023
The GDPR applies to the collection of identifiable images
Registration and A1/A3 certificates issued by another EU/EEA member state are valid in Romania, with no need for a new registration — under the mutual recognition principle of EU Regulation 2019/947.
